Import GHAP High-Resolution Pollution Data for Brazilian Municipalities

Source: R/sus_grid_pollution_ghap.R
sus_grid_pollution_ghap.Rd

sus_grid_pollution_ghap() downloads, crops, spatially aggregates, and caches GHAP (GlobalHighAirPollutants) raster data to Brazilian municipalities. No API key is required.

GHAP provides AI-generated, seamless ground-level air pollutant fields at 1 km (PM2.5, CO) and 10 km (O3) resolution. Files are downloaded as NetCDF from Zenodo, cropped to Brazil, aggregated with area-weighted extraction, and the result is stored as a Parquet cache for fast subsequent access.

Available pollutants and temporal coverage:

  • PM2.5 ("pm25") – annual only (V2), 2000-2022, 1 km, \(\mu g/m^3\)

  • O3 ("o3") – annual only, 2000-2020, 10 km, ppb

  • CO ("co") – annual only, 2019-2022, 1 km, mg/m\(^3\)

  • NO2 ("no2") – data not yet publicly released

When municipalities is provided the function returns a climasus_df at stage = "climate", type = "pollution_ghap", compatible with sus_climate_anomaly(), sus_climate_aggregate(), and sus_mod_dlnm().

Usage

sus_grid_pollution_ghap(
  pollutants = "pm25",
  resolution = "monthly",
  years = NULL,
  months = 1:12,
  municipalities = NULL,
  raster_area = FALSE,
  agg_fun = "mean",
  crop_brazil = TRUE,
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/ghap",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

pollutants

Character vector, or the single string "all" (= all three below). Accepted: "pm25" (default), "o3", "co"; e.g. c("pm25", "o3"). "no2" is dropped with a warning (not released); other values error, and error if nothing valid remains.

resolution

Character scalar: "daily", "monthly" (default) or "annual" (other values error). Currently every supported pollutant is only served annually, so "daily" and "monthly" fall back to "annual" with a warning; the annual value is assigned to January 1st of each year. (Legacy daily/monthly PM2.5 ZIP handling remains in the code but is not reachable.)

years

Numeric vector or NULL. Accepted forms: scalar (2020), range (2018:2022) or explicit vector (c(2019, 2022) = exactly those two years, NOT the range – use 2019:2022). Per pollutant (annual): PM2.5 2000-2022, O3 2000-2020, CO 2019-2022. Years unavailable for a pollutant are NOT an error: a warning is issued and they are dropped (a pollutant with no valid year is skipped). NULL (default) = all available years of each pollutant.

months

Numeric vector of months (1-12), e.g. 1:3, c(1, 7). Default 1:12. Only relevant for monthly/daily source files, which are not served currently (annual fallback), so it has no practical effect. Values outside 1-12 or NA error.

municipalities

An sf polygon object (e.g. from geobr::read_municipality()) or NULL (default). Non-sf input errors. When provided, requires terra and exactextractr; rasters are aggregated per polygon and a climasus_df is returned. If NULL, file paths or a SpatRaster are returned (see raster_area).

raster_area

Only used when municipalities = NULL. One of:

  • FALSE (default) – return the character vector of cached file paths.

  • TRUE – return an in-memory terra::SpatRaster, full extent.

  • an sf POLYGON object – return the SpatRaster cropped and masked to that area.

  • a 2-letter Brazilian state code (e.g. "MT") – auto-download the state boundary via geobr (cached) and crop/mask to it.

Ignored (file-path behavior takes precedence) if municipalities is provided.

IMPORTANT limitation: for resolution = "daily" requests, each monthly ZIP contains one NetCDF file per day. Extracting and stacking every daily file into the returned raster would require decompressing multi-gigabyte archives on every call, so this option instead extracts and returns only the FIRST available day of each requested pollutant/month as a representative sample – the returned raster is NOT the full daily time series. Users who need the complete daily series should extract the cached ZIP themselves (see the file paths returned when raster_area = FALSE), or request narrower month ranges and read the daily NetCDF files directly. For "monthly" and "annual" resolutions the underlying NetCDF file is read directly (no ZIP involved), but only its first layer is used per requested pollutant/month/year for the same reason: to keep this option lightweight and predictable rather than silently building a large multi-day stack.

agg_fun

Character scalar. Spatial aggregation for exactextractr::exact_extract(): "mean" (default, area-weighted), "sum", "median", "min" or "max"; other values error. Also names the output column (<pollutant>_<agg_fun>, e.g. pm25_mean).

crop_brazil

Logical scalar. Crop global rasters to Brazil's bounding box before extraction (lower memory). Default TRUE.

use_cache

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), reuse downloaded NetCDF files and municipality-level Parquet caches; FALSE recomputes.

cache_dir

Character scalar. Root cache directory, with one sub-directory per pollutant. Default "~/.climasus4r_cache/ghap".

lang

Character scalar. Message language: "pt" (default), "en" or "es"; other values error.

verbose

Logical scalar. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

  • If municipalities is provided: a climasus_df tibble with columns code_muni, date, and one column per pollutant (e.g., pm25_mean, o3_mean). Metadata: stage = "climate", type = "pollution_ghap".

  • If municipalities = NULL: a named character vector of paths to the cached NetCDF files, or, per raster_area, an in-memory terra::SpatRaster with one layer per requested pollutant/month, each layer being a single representative day (see raster_area for details and limitations), optionally cropped and masked to an area of interest.

Data source

Wei, J. et al. (2023). Estimating 1-km-resolution PM2.5 concentrations across China using the space-time random forest approach. Remote Sensing of Environment, 231, 111221. DOI: doi:10.5281/zenodo.10800980
Wei, J. et al. GlobalHighAirPollutants (GHAP) v2. Zenodo. CC-BY 4.0.
PM2.5: doi:10.5281/zenodo.10800980 | O3: doi:10.5281/zenodo.10208188 | CO: doi:10.5281/zenodo.14207363

Packages required

Spatial aggregation requires terra and exactextractr (both in Suggests). The Parquet cache requires arrow (in Imports). Install with install.packages(c("terra", "exactextractr")).

See also

sus_grid_pollution_cams(), sus_grid_pollution_merra2(), sus_grid_era5(), sus_grid_join(), sus_grid_plot(), sus_climate_anomaly(), sus_climate_aggregate(), sus_mod_dlnm()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(geobr)
mt_mun <- read_municipality(code_muni = "MT", year = 2020)

# PM2.5 for Mato Grosso, 2020 (monthly requests fall back to annual)
ghap <- sus_grid_pollution_ghap(
  pollutants    = "pm25",
  resolution    = "monthly",
  years         = 2020,
  months        = 1:3,
  municipalities = mt_mun,
  lang          = "pt"
)

sus_meta(ghap, "stage")  # "climate"
sus_meta(ghap, "type")   # "pollution_ghap"

# O3 annual, all available years
ghap_o3 <- sus_grid_pollution_ghap(
  pollutants    = "o3",
  resolution    = "annual",
  municipalities = mt_mun,
  lang          = "en"
)
} # }
